reports.specimen_type: Breast, left modified radical mastectomy with axillary dissection
reports.brief: A 52-year-old woman with a palpable left breast lump underwent modified radical mastectomy with level I-II axillary dissection after a core biopsy showed carcinoma. The report describes invasive breast carcinoma of no special type, Nottingham grade 2, 32 mm in greatest dimension, with metastatic carcinoma in 3 of 14 axillary lymph nodes and no extranodal extension. All margins are free, the closest being the deep margin at 6 mm; lymphovascular invasion is present and perineural invasion absent; pT2 pN1a.

reports.specimen_type: Colon, right hemicolectomy
reports.brief: Right hemicolectomy for a caecal mass found during work-up of iron deficiency anaemia. Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the caecum, 45 mm, invading through the muscularis propria into pericolic fat without serosal involvement (pT3). Two of 18 regional lymph nodes contain metastatic carcinoma (pN1b); proximal, distal and radial margins are clear, lymphovascular invasion is present and perineural invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Rectum, low anterior resection
reports.brief: Low anterior resection without neoadjuvant therapy for an upper rectal adenocarcinoma found on screening colonoscopy. Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, 30 mm, invading into but not through the muscularis propria (pT2), with 0 of 15 lymph nodes involved (pN0). Circumferential resection margin 4 mm and distal margin 25 mm, both clear; no lymphovascular or perineural invasion.

reports.specimen_type: Stomach, distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy
reports.brief: Distal gastrectomy with D2 lymph node dissection for an ulcerating antral mass. Intestinal-type adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, 50 mm, invading the subserosal connective tissue without penetrating the visceral peritoneum (pT3). Metastatic carcinoma in 5 of 22 lymph nodes (pN2); margins free with the closest (proximal) at 30 mm; lymphovascular and perineural invasion both present.

reports.specimen_type: Tongue, right partial glossectomy with selective neck dissection
reports.brief: Right partial glossectomy with ipsilateral selective neck dissection (levels I-IV) for an ulcer on the lateral border of the tongue in a man with a long history of tobacco chewing. Moderately differentiated keratinising squamous cell carcinoma, 28 mm, depth of invasion 7 mm (pT2). One of 24 neck nodes involved, the deposit 18 mm without extranodal extension (pN1); closest mucosal margin 6 mm and deep margin 5 mm, perineural invasion present, lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Thyroid, total thyroidectomy with central compartment dissection
reports.brief: Total thyroidectomy with central compartment neck dissection for a right thyroid nodule reported as Bethesda VI on fine-needle aspiration. Papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic subtype, 24 mm, confined to the right lobe without extrathyroidal extension (pT2). One of 6 level VI lymph nodes contains metastatic carcinoma (pN1a); margins clear, lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Kidney, left radical nephrectomy
reports.brief: Left radical nephrectomy for an incidentally detected renal mass. Clear cell renal cell carcinoma, WHO/ISUP grade 2, 65 mm, confined to the kidney with no renal sinus or perinephric fat invasion (pT1b). Two hilar lymph nodes are free of tumour (pN0); renal vein, ureteric and Gerota fascia margins are clear and lymphovascular invasion is absent.

reports.specimen_type: Uterus, total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy
reports.brief: Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy for postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 1, 35 mm, invading less than half of the myometrium (8 of 20 mm) with no cervical stromal involvement (pT1a). Zero of 12 pelvic lymph nodes involved (pN0); adnexa uninvolved, lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Cervix, radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy
reports.brief: Radical hysterectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy for a cervical growth seen on speculum examination. Moderately differentiated non-keratinising squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, 32 mm, stromal invasion 11 of 15 mm, confined to the cervix (pT1b1). Two of 20 pelvic lymph nodes contain metastatic carcinoma (pN1); vaginal cuff and parametrial margins clear, lymphovascular invasion present, perineural invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Lung, right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node sampling
reports.brief: Right upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node sampling for a peripheral lung nodule in a former smoker. Invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma, acinar predominant, 28 mm, with no visceral pleural invasion (pT1c). Zero of 9 hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes involved (pN0); bronchial and vascular margins clear, lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Lymph node, left cervical excision biopsy
reports.brief: Excision biopsy of an enlarging 30 mm left cervical lymph node in a man with fever, night sweats and weight loss. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, germinal centre B-cell-like by the Hans algorithm. Immunohistochemistry: CD20 and PAX5 positive, CD3 negative, CD10 positive, BCL6 positive, MUM1 negative, BCL2 positive, Ki-67 about 80 percent. Synoptic elements that do not apply to a lymph node biopsy are recorded as Not applicable.

reports.specimen_type: Skin, excision of a pigmented lesion of the upper back
reports.brief: Excision of a 14 mm irregular pigmented lesion on the upper back that had changed over six months. Invasive melanoma, superficial spreading type, Breslow thickness 1.6 mm, Clark level IV, no ulceration, mitotic rate 2 per mm2 (pT2a). Immunohistochemistry: SOX10, Melan-A and HMB-45 positive, pancytokeratin negative. Peripheral margin 4 mm and deep margin 3 mm clear, no lymphovascular or perineural invasion, no lymph nodes submitted.

reports.specimen_type: Liver, ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a hepatic mass
reports.brief: Ultrasound-guided core biopsy of multiple liver lesions in a man with weight loss and no known primary tumour. Metastatic poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma infiltrating liver parenchyma. Immunohistochemistry: CK7 positive, CK20 negative, TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, CDX2 negative and HepPar-1 negative, supporting a lung primary. Synoptic elements that do not apply to a core biopsy are recorded as Not applicable.

reports.specimen_type: Stomach, laparoscopic wedge resection of a gastric wall mass
reports.brief: Laparoscopic wedge resection of a 55 mm submucosal mass of the gastric body. Gastrointestinal stromal tumour, spindle cell type, 3 mitoses per 5 mm2, serosa intact (pT3). Immunohistochemistry: CD117 and DOG1 diffusely positive, CD34 positive, desmin, S100 and SMA negative. Resection margins free with the closest at 8 mm; no lymph nodes submitted; lymphovascular and perineural invasion not identified.

reports.specimen_type: Breast, right wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy
reports.brief: Right wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy for a screen-detected lesion. Invasive lobular carcinoma, classic type, Nottingham grade 2, 18 mm (pT1c); immunohistochemistry shows E-cadherin negative, ER positive (Allred 8), PR positive (Allred 6) and HER2 negative (score 1+). Sentinel lymph nodes 0 of 2 (pN0(sn)); all margins clear with the closest (superior) at 3 mm; lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Prostate, radical prostatectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy
reports.brief: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection for biopsy-proven prostate cancer with a PSA of 8.4 ng/mL. Acinar adenocarcinoma, Gleason score 3+4=7 (Grade Group 2), involving about 15 percent of the gland, organ-confined without extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion (pT2). Zero of 8 pelvic lymph nodes involved (pN0); surgical margins negative, perineural invasion present, lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Urinary bladder, transurethral resection of bladder tumour
reports.brief: Transurethral resection of a papillary bladder tumour in a man with painless haematuria. Invasive high-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma invading the lamina propria; muscularis propria is present in the specimen and free of tumour (pT1). No lymphovascular invasion; tumour size and margins are not assessable in a transurethral specimen and pN is recorded as Not applicable.

reports.specimen_type: Ovary, hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy
reports.brief: Total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy for a right adnexal mass. High-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary, 75 mm, capsule intact and surface uninvolved, omentum and peritoneal washings negative (pT1a). Immunohistochemistry: WT1 and PAX8 positive, p53 aberrant (diffuse strong). Zero of 10 pelvic lymph nodes involved (pN0).

reports.specimen_type: Gallbladder, extended cholecystectomy with hepatic wedge
reports.brief: Extended cholecystectomy with a hepatic wedge for gallbladder wall thickening in a woman with long-standing gallstones. Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder fundus, 22 mm, invading the perimuscular connective tissue on the peritoneal side without involving the serosa (pT2a). Cystic duct and hepatic bed margins clear; 0 of 4 lymph nodes involved (pN0); lymphovascular invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Oesophagus, Ivor Lewis oesophagectomy
reports.brief: Ivor Lewis oesophagectomy without neoadjuvant therapy for a mid-thoracic oesophageal stricture. Moderately differentiated keratinising squamous cell carcinoma, 40 mm, invading the adventitia (pT3). One of 16 regional lymph nodes contains metastatic carcinoma (pN1); proximal, distal and circumferential margins clear, lymphovascular invasion present, perineural invasion absent.

reports.specimen_type: Testis, right radical inguinal orchidectomy
reports.brief: Right radical inguinal orchidectomy for a painless testicular swelling with raised LDH and normal AFP. Classic seminoma, 38 mm, confined to the testis, no lymphovascular or rete testis invasion, spermatic cord margin clear (pT1b, pure seminoma 3 cm or larger). Immunohistochemistry: OCT3/4, SALL4 and CD117 positive, CD30 and AFP negative. No lymph nodes submitted (pNX).

reports.specimen_type: Pancreas, pancreaticoduodenectomy
reports.brief: Pancreaticoduodenectomy for obstructive jaundice due to a pancreatic head mass. Moderately differentiated ductal adenocarcinoma, 26 mm (pT2), with metastatic carcinoma in 3 of 17 regional lymph nodes (pN1). Superior mesenteric artery margin 2 mm, pancreatic neck and bile duct margins clear; perineural and lymphovascular invasion both present.

reports.specimen_type: Colon, laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy
reports.brief: Laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy for a sigmoid adenocarcinoma diagnosed on colonoscopic biopsy. Well to moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, 25 mm, invading into but not through the muscularis propria (pT2), with 0 of 14 lymph nodes involved (pN0). Proximal, distal and mesenteric margins clear; no lymphovascular or perineural invasion.

A 34-year-old woman with menorrhagia, fatigue and breathlessness on exertion. Severe microcytic hypochromic anaemia with haemoglobin about 6.2 g/dL, MCV in the low 60s fL, a raised RDW and a reactive platelet count near 480 x10^9/L; white cells normal. Haemoglobin is at a critical level, so the comment must flag it and recommend urgent clinical review and iron studies.

reports.scenario: Absolute lymphocytosis suggestive of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia
reports.brief: A 58-year-old man with small cervical lymph nodes and a raised white cell count on a routine health check. Absolute lymphocytosis with total white cells around 48 x10^9/L and lymphocytes about 82 percent; haemoglobin and platelets within or just below the reference range. No critical value is present; the interpretation suggests peripheral smear review and flow cytometry.

A 45-year-old woman with petechiae and gum bleeding for three days. Isolated severe thrombocytopenia with platelets about 12 x10^9/L and a high MPV; haemoglobin, red-cell indices and white cells normal. The platelet count is a critical value: the comment must flag it and recommend urgent clinician notification and a peripheral smear to exclude pseudothrombocytopenia.

reports.scenario: Macrocytic anaemia with mild leukopenia and thrombocytopenia
reports.brief: A 67-year-old strict vegetarian man with fatigue, paraesthesia and glossitis. Macrocytic anaemia with haemoglobin about 7.8 g/dL and MCV around 118 fL, with mild leukopenia (white cells about 3.2 x10^9/L) and mild thrombocytopenia (about 110 x10^9/L), a pattern suggestive of vitamin B12 deficiency. No critical value is present; recommend serum vitamin B12 and folate levels.

A 29-year-old woman with fever ten days after a cycle of chemotherapy for breast cancer. White cells about 0.9 x10^9/L with neutrophils about 22 percent, giving an absolute neutrophil count near 0.2 x10^9/L; mild normocytic anaemia and platelets about 95 x10^9/L. The absolute neutrophil count is a critical value: the comment must flag it and recommend urgent assessment for febrile neutropenia.

A 41-year-old man with fever and a productive cough for four days. Neutrophilic leukocytosis with white cells about 18.6 x10^9/L and neutrophils about 86 percent, relative lymphopenia, normal haemoglobin and a normal platelet count. No critical value is present; the interpretation notes a pattern consistent with acute bacterial infection.

A 72-year-old man with headaches, a plethoric face and itching after bathing. Marked erythrocytosis with haemoglobin about 20.4 g/dL and haematocrit about 61 percent, normal red-cell indices, mild leukocytosis and platelets around 520 x10^9/L. The haematocrit is a critical value: the comment must flag it and recommend urgent haematology referral, JAK2 testing and consideration of venesection.

reports.scenario: Normal blood count at a pre-employment check
reports.brief: A healthy 26-year-old woman with no symptoms having a pre-employment health check. All values within the adult female reference ranges: haemoglobin about 13.2 g/dL, normal red-cell indices, white cells about 6.8 x10^9/L with a normal differential and platelets about 260 x10^9/L. No critical value is present; the interpretation states a normal blood count.

A 52-year-old man with seasonal allergic rhinitis attending a routine review. Haemoglobin, red-cell indices, total white cells (about 7.2 x10^9/L) and platelets within reference ranges, with mild eosinophilia (eosinophils about 9 percent, absolute about 0.65 x10^9/L). No critical value is present; the interpretation suggests correlation with the allergy history and a stool examination for parasites.

reports.scenario: Microcytosis with a high red cell count (beta-thalassaemia trait pattern)
reports.brief: A 63-year-old woman with lifelong mild anaemia and no history of bleeding. Mild microcytic anaemia with haemoglobin about 11.2 g/dL, MCV around 64 fL, a red cell count about 5.6 x10^12/L and a normal RDW, a pattern suggestive of beta-thalassaemia trait rather than iron deficiency. White cells and platelets normal; no critical value is present; recommend haemoglobin HPLC.

reports.scenario: Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia in dengue fever
reports.brief: A 38-year-old man on day five of a febrile illness with NS1-positive dengue. Leukopenia with white cells about 2.8 x10^9/L, platelets about 38 x10^9/L and a haematocrit about 48 percent at the upper end of the range, suggesting haemoconcentration; haemoglobin about 16.0 g/dL. No critical value is present; the comment recommends daily platelet and haematocrit monitoring.
